source.name: BBC World News RSS
source.title: Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect
source.summary: Germany has blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport but there has been a series of suspicious incidents elsewhere.

lesson.title: A series of suspected attacks
lesson.overview: Read carefully when responsibility is uncertain.
lesson.prediction: Read the title. What do you think the story is about?
discussion: What happened? Start with: The report says ___.
Complete: To check a news claim, I would look for ___.
news_brief_sentences: The report describes suspected attacks in Europe.
Germany has blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport.
Other suspicious incidents have happened elsewhere.
Russia is the main suspect in the report.

vocabulary.definition: making people think something may be wrong
a person or party thought to be responsible

grammar.explanation: In the report limits the statement to what this source says. Suspect does not mean proven responsible.
grammar.example_quote: Russia is the main suspect in the report.

quiz.question: Which location is specifically named?
options: Leipzig airport
Every European capital
A port in France
option_feedback: Leipzig airport is the named location.
The source does not name every capital.
This port is not identified in the source.

quiz.question: What does the source say about incidents elsewhere?
options: There has been a series of suspicious incidents.
It gives the exact details of every incident.
It says no other incidents occurred.
option_feedback: That is the limited information in the summary.
The supplied summary does not contain every detail.
This contradicts the mention of other incidents.

quiz.question: What does suspicious mean?
options: Giving reason to think something may be wrong
Proven harmless in every case
Fully explained beyond doubt
option_feedback: Suspicious expresses concern or doubt.
Harmless is not the meaning of suspicious.
Suspicion differs from complete certainty.

quiz.question: Does main suspect mean proven responsible?
options: No. Suspicion is not proof.
Yes. The two expressions mean the same.
No. It means responsibility is impossible.
option_feedback: Being suspected does not establish guilt.
These expressions have different meanings.
A suspicion does not rule responsibility out.
